captures.description: THE EVENT, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'NaNoGenMo (National Novel Generation Month) is an annual programming challenge where participants spend the month of November writing computer code to procedurally generate a novel of 50,000 or more words.' The core goal and rules (the period to the minute; 'Definition of a Novel: The definition is flexible'; 'Respect for copyright applies.'; sharing text and code; joining by a GitHub issue); background (a 'playful programming spoof of NaNoWriMo'; edition repositories 'spanning from 2013 onward, managed by maintainers like Darius Kazemi and Hugo van Kemenade'); an offer on participating or on techniques. Six cards: the NaNoGenMo site, Reddit, GitHub, Liza Daly, centerconsulting.com, a YouTube video; the paste ends on the video card.

atoms.evidence: NaNoGenMo (National Novel Generation Month) is an annual programming challenge
managed by maintainers like Darius Kazemi and Hugo van Kemenade
Write and run code between November 1 (12:01 am GMT) and December 1 (12:01 am GMT) to output a text work of 50,000+ words.
Participants share both the generated text and the source code at the end of the event.
Created as a playful programming spoof of NaNoWriMo (National Novel Writing Month)
